marketInsightsHtml: La charge de base allemande du 26 novembre a grimpé de 12,80 € pour s'établir à 219,70 €/MWh, tandis que la charge de novembre française a bondi d'un record de 16,70 € à 207,45 €/MWh. Les livraisons rapides ont également rebondi par rapport aux plus bas du week-end, le Day-Ahead allemand ayant atteint 34,51 € à 155,11 €/MWh, la France à 161,53 €/MWh et le N2EX britannique à 108,17 £/MWh.

marketInsights.gas:
European natural gas rallied sharply on Monday before seeing a mild diplomatic pullback to around €95/MWh this morning. Dutch TTF November 26 settled up €3.90 on Monday at €96.70/MWh with Day-Ahead jumping €5.00 to €97.80/MWh. In the UK, NBP Day-Ahead surged 13.54p to 237.29p/th, while November 26 gained 10.23p to settle at 238.45p/th, with intraday highs testing 240p/th.

The complex remains underpinned by physical supply disruptions in the Middle East, where maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz remains heavily compromised by recurring attacks on commercial shipping, keeping roughly 80% of Persian Gulf LNG flows locked away from international markets. However, benchmark contracts took a temporary breather following news that senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan met with top Iranian leaders in Tehran on Monday to de-escalate regional hostilities, with Tehran describing the discussions as "very good". Competition for uncommitted Atlantic LNG continues to simmer as Asian buyers seek replacement volumes, while front month Brent crude trades around $115/bbl as participants wait to see whether US strikes resume following next week's midterm elections.

Upstream supply remains constrained by unplanned Norwegian outages at Oseberg and Åsgard, which lifted offline capacity to 40 mcm/d on Monday and reduced Emden flows to 69 mcm/d.

Total EU storage stands at 74.92% (848.6 TWh), with Germany lagging at 61.65% and the UK at 40.51%. While a brief mid-week warming is capping prompt heating offtake, weather models show an abrupt drop from Thursday as a blocking high pressure brings colder air and fog into early November.
marketInsights.power:
European forward power curves surged to fresh multi-year highs on Monday, tracking gas strength alongside forecasts of collapsing wind and colder temperatures. German November 26 baseload climbed €12.80 to settle at €219.70/MWh, while French November jumped a record €16.70 to €207.45/MWh. UK November 26 added £10.25 to close at a new high of £190.50/MWh. Prompt delivery also rebounded from weekend lows with German Day-Ahead cleared up €34.51 at €155.11/MWh, France rose to €161.53/MWh, and UK N2EX climbed to £108.17/MWh.

Renewable generation faces an acute slump later this week. Following weekend storms where German wind averaged over 44 GW, expanding high pressure will cause wind output across Northwest Europe to plunge to 3–6% load factors by Thursday to Saturday (dropping below 3 GW in Germany and 4 GW in the UK), triggering severe Dunkelflaute balancing requirements.

Supply fundamentals remain structurally tight despite minor nuclear relief. While Belgium's Doel 4 and Tihange 3 ramped back up to full output over the weekend, Doel 4 disconnected again for maintenance until 1 November. In the UK, high weekend wind forced NESO to accept significant wind curtailments while paying gas-fired plants to balance constraints in the south. Thermal generation margins continue to heavily favour coal, with German November 40% coal dark spreads widening their advantage over clean sparks to nearly €87/MWh (€95.43/MWh dark vs. €8.69/MWh spark).
